ROOT CAUSE (ties back to exp014's error analysis): pseudo-labels came from the CONFIDENT region (<0.02 or >0.98 predicted probability), which exp014 showed is exactly where the model already has near-zero error (>9h screen_time, near-deterministic labels). Adding more near-duplicate-information rows from a region the model already nails doesn't help, and may add a small amount of confirmation-bias noise (model reinforcing its own confident-but-not-perfectly-correct predictions) -- consistent with the slightly negative (though noise-floor) delta. LESSON: pseudo-labeling is most useful when confident predictions come from an under-sampled or genuinely uncertain-but-resolvable region; here the confident region is already both correct and heavily represented in the original 691k training rows, so there's no real information to add. FINAL DECISION: pseudo-labeling lever closed, no further variants planned (e.g. lower confidence threshold would only worsen label quality, not fix the underlying issue).

Contrasts sharply with exp010 (-0.00033 for 2-way pairwise products, which trees reconstruct trivially). LESSON: the depth of interaction matters -- trees handle 2-way interactions for free but 3+-way ratios/interactions can still be worth hand-engineering even for tree models.
